methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Young workers facing AI displacement pressure without corresponding deep skill-building infrastructure signals shallow anxiety rather than distributed capability development, risking neither depth nor breadth in workforce adaptation.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents peer-network skill transfer outside traditional tech hubs, testing whether deep capability can emerge through distributed, place-based learning models rather than platform delivery.

signals.title: Comcast, Appalachian Power continue wrangling over broadband expansion
signals.signal_reading: Infrastructure disputes blocking broadband deployment in Appalachian Virginia prevent even shallow platform-based AI adoption, reinforcing the foundation for concentrated capability by limiting rural access to basic connectivity prerequisites.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon's $500M Scale AI expansion and TurbineOne HQ relocation to NoVA deepens defense-AI concentration in the metro corridor, channeling federal investment toward existing capability centers rather than distributing expertise regionally.

signals.title: Roanoke College president: Virginia’s future workforce depends on fixing the path from college to career - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College president's emphasis on fixing college-to-career pathways signals recognition that distributed AI fluency requires institutional bridges beyond metro areas, positioning regional colleges as potential nodes for peer-based skill networks rather than platform dependency.
